title: fix(sharing): a declared sharing rule grants in an organization created after boot, without a restart
body:
Fixes #36982
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 新建的组织(例如新环境的第一次注册)里,应用自带的共享规则从创建那一刻就生效,被指派人立即能看到并编辑任务,不再需要重启服务器。
- 属于平台记录共享这条线,替任务与备忘那张卡(内置任务对象的被指派人授权)解决新组织里授权缺失的问题。
- 出错时表现为新组织里某条应用自带规则没有授权(只会少给,不会多给;每个组织的授权仍只落在本组织内);这次改动可以直接撤回,撤回后回到重启才生效的旧行为。
- 无

## What changes

`SharingServicePlugin` bound its per-record rule hooks once at boot, on the objects of the rules it served then. Under a walled posture a declared rule is served once per organization that exists (ADR-0131 D2), so a kernel that booted with no organization bound no hook on a declared rule's object. The organization-created middleware (`addDeclaredRuleScope`) added the new organization's scope and bound nothing, so a record written in that organization got no `sys_record_share` grant until the next restart. It under-granted; it never over-granted.

- `SharingRuleService.listRuleHookObjects()` (new): the objects the record hooks bind on — every object an active `sys_sharing_rule` row names, plus every object an active DECLARATION names, whatever organizations serve it at that moment and whatever the activation ledger says of it. The binding is per object and organization-agnostic; the organization is resolved when a record is evaluated (`evaluateAllForRecord` lists the projections live, each sweeping inside its own organization at the driver), so isolation is unchanged.
- `rule-hooks.ts`: new `rebindRuleHooks(engine, service, logger)` reads `listRuleHookObjects()`, then unbinds and calls `bindRuleHooks` with that object set; the read runs before the unbind, so a failed read keeps the previous bindings (as before). `bindRuleHooks`' `rules` parameter widens to the two fields it reads (`object_name`, `active`), a non-breaking widening; its hook bodies are unchanged and stay in that symbol (the system-context census row keys the `afterDelete` elevation read to it).
- `sharing-plugin.ts`: boot and the `sys_sharing_rule` data-change rebind both go through one private `bindRuleHooks` method (the binding site ADR-0057 anchors as `sharing-plugin.ts#bindRuleHooks`), which calls `rebindRuleHooks`, so the two cannot derive different object sets. The organization-created middleware is unchanged: it still adds the scope, and the hooks already bound now serve it.
- Same derivation closes the sibling shape: a declared rule switched off in the activation ledger at boot and on later keeps its object bound (the ledger reconcile never rebinds).

Why per object rather than a rebind in the organization-created middleware: a rebind there would re-derive the hook set from the served projections each time, which is exactly the snapshot that drifted (and an unknown-scope boot, or a ledger switch, would still bind nothing). Binding from the declaration cannot drift with the organizations at all. A hook on an object no projection serves yet evaluates no rule and grants nothing.

## Tests

- `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/declared-rule-late-organization.test.ts` (new, real stack, ONE boot): `ObjectKernel` + `ObjectQLPlugin` over better-sqlite3 + `SharingServicePlugin`, `isolated` posture (the `tenancy` service plus the engine posture accessor the security plugin hands it), a package-declared `field` rule (`assignee_id`, edit) on a private object; every organization is inserted after `bootstrap()`.
  - Case 1: in the first organization created after boot, a task's assignee gets exactly one edit grant from the declared rule and reads the record; a member the rule does not name still reads nothing. RED on origin/main `57445a69981` (`expected [] to deeply equal [ ObjectContaining ]`), green with the fix.
  - Case 2 (isolation, both directions): organization A authors its own rule on the same object; control — it grants on A's record; B's record matching A's criteria gets exactly one grant, B's projection of the declared rule, stamped `organization_id` B; A's watcher does not read it. Green on origin/main and with the fix.
- `sharing-rule.test.ts` (walled describe): `listRuleHookObjects()` names the declared rule's object with no scope, with unknown scopes, and with the rule switched off in the ledger (while `listRules` serves nothing in each); a stored row's object joins; an inactive declaration binds nothing.
- `rule-rebind.test.ts`: mocks moved from `listRules` to `listRuleHookObjects`, the rebind seam's new read; assertions unchanged.
- Ablation at head `e67a0507ced` (fix committed first; `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, anchor x1 to x0, blob `6558c83dc6c3` to `d440ba76857c`): the declaration loop in `listRuleHookObjects` removed, so only served projections bind. Over the three touched suites: `Tests 2 failed | 160 passed` — exactly the two new pins (the one-boot late-organization case and the `listRuleHookObjects` pin). Restored: blob `6558c83dc6c3` equals the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty. No dist rebuild needed: the suites import the subject from `src`.
- At head `e67a0507ced`: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing test` — Test Files 78 passed, Tests 1629 passed, 11 skipped; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing typecheck` — exit 0, `check:test-typecheck: OK` (the new test is in the `tsconfig.test.json` program, `--listFilesOnly` 1 hit).

<details><summary>Derived gates at e67a0507ced</summary>

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (7 paths vs merge base `57445a699`): 73 families, all run after a full `pnpm build` (120 tasks, lock VERDICT command-exit 0), each exit captured before any pipe: 73 exit 0. `--ran`: 73 derived, 73 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN (exit 0). On the first pass two families were red and are green now: `check:adr-symbol-anchors` (ADR-0057 anchors the plugin's binding site as `sharing-plugin.ts#bindRuleHooks`; kept as the private method) and `check:system-context-census` (row 31 keys the rule hooks' `afterDelete` elevation read to `bindRuleHooks`; the hook bodies stay in that symbol). `test:repo` is CI's (Test Core).

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- PR #36965's runtime test boots twice because of this defect. With this fix on `main`, one boot should do: the declared `sys_task_assignee` object is bound at boot from the declaration, and the organization inserted afterwards is served by those hooks. Not measured here (that test lives in plugin-security on #36965's branch, outside this card's surface); left to #36942's follow-up.
- A composition with `SharingServicePlugin` but no engine posture accessor (no security plugin) reads its sharing posture as walled while the engine applies no tenant scope, so an organization-authored rule's per-record pass matches records of other organizations there. Seen while building this fixture; the fixture now sets the posture as a deployment does. No tenant wall exists in that composition either, so nothing crosses one; noted, not filed.

## Verification

Read first: `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-rule-service.ts` (`listRuleHookObjects`, the derivation), `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/rule-hooks.ts` (`rebindRuleHooks`), `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts` (the private `bindRuleHooks` and its two callers).

Two minutes: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-sharing exec vitest run src/declared-rule-late-organization.test.ts` — expect 2 passed; on `origin/main` the first case fails with no grant row.
